audit.whatIsWrong: Level chart disagreed across layers: content win[] read Lux/Lux/Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Viktor (matching the packet levelChart) while every full-layer phases[N].side read 'Skill'. Rows 0, 1 and 6 rendered two different answers.
audit.why: Lux Q reaches 1175 and E 1100; Viktor's Q is 600 and his E cast range 525, so levels 1-2 are hers on range alone. Late, augmented Hextech Ray plus Arcane Storm (120/100/80s) hold zones a single 60/50/40s Final Spark cannot, which is why the packet chart and content layer both give 2+ items to Viktor.
audit.corrected: phases[0].side and phases[1].side moved to 'Lux', phases[6].side moved to 'Viktor', each with its why rewritten in the same proposal. No content-layer win[N] edit is proposed because win[0]='Lux', win[1]='Lux' and win[6]='Viktor' ALREADY hold the target values — a before==after edit would be rejected. After these edits the two layers agree on all seven rows.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.spikes and spikes[] described Viktor's scaling with the wrong ability names and no reference to his actual spike mechanism.
audit.why: Viktor's power steps come from Glorious Evolution: every 100 Hex Fragments permanently augments one ability. His first augment is the real lane spike, not an item timing. Lux's spikes stay Lost Chapter, level 6 (Final Spark 60s at rank 1) and Luden's.
audit.corrected: breakdown.spikes now names the 100-Fragment augment; spikes[0..3] use Hextech Ray and Arcane Storm and carry real cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both of Viktor's key abilities were named wrong throughout the content layer: 'Death Ray' for E (really Hextech Ray) and 'Chaos Storm' for R (really Arcane Storm). The auto-attack-reset tell on Siphon Power was absent entirely.
audit.why: Riot's kit file gives Q Siphon Power (9/8/7/6/5s, 600 range, shield + empowered next attack = an auto reset), W Gravity Field (17/16/15/14/13s, 800, slow into stun), E Hextech Ray (12/11/10/9/8s, 525 cast, line), R Arcane Storm (120/100/80s, 700, redirectable zone). Lux answers with Q 10s/1175 root, E 10/9.5/9/8.5/8s/1100 slow zone, W 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s shield, R 60/50/40s at 3340. The decisive interaction is range: every trade Viktor wants requires him to walk from 800 into Lux's 1100-1175 band, and his combo opens with the Siphon Power auto-reset wind-up, which is the visible cue to step back.
audit.corrected: All 'Death Ray' and 'Chaos Storm' references replaced; dosFull[1].d now states the Illumination passive weave; breakdown.cooldowns now carries Gravity Field 17s->13s, Siphon Power 9s, Lux Q 10s and R 60s.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit at all (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT).
audit.why: It is the field that exists to hold real numbers.
audit.corrected: Rewritten with Gravity Field 17s rank 1 / 13s rank 5, Siphon Power 9s, Lux Q 10s and Final Spark 60s.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was the tradeGood string verbatim and dontsFull[2].d was the tradeBad string verbatim, both under unrelated titles (lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED). dosFull[0].d and dontsFull[0].d were likewise bodies that did not answer their own titles.
audit.why: The title promises one thing and the body explains another.
audit.corrected: All four bodies rewritten to match their titles, grounded in this matchup's ranges and cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[10].t contained 'ping your jungler every Mantra' — Mantra is Karma's mechanic, a template leak from another champion's page.
audit.why: Lux has no Mantra; the cycle in question is Final Spark's 60s.
Nothing in the brief indicates a 26.15 change to either kit; live patch is 26.15 and no patch-sensitivity claim is written into the page.

edits.before: - Viktor Gravity Field: matchup-defining — The stun zone owns every all-in — walk out the moment it drops or fight outside it. Count it out loud if you must. - Your W Prismatic Barrier has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.

edits.before: The stun zone owns every all-in — walk out the moment it drops or fight outside it. Bait it, count it, then go.
edits.after: His Q reaches only 600, so drop E on his farm spot from outside it — the slow plus an Illumination auto is free chip.

edits.before: E the contact, detonate, weave the passive auto, and keep Q visibly loaded — the chip is free and the root threat does the zoning.
edits.after: Every spell charges Illumination; the follow-up auto ignites it for bonus magic damage, so take one auto after each E detonation.

edits.before: Viktor burns Gravity Field on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: Gravity Field on nothing is a 13-to-17 second invitation — walk up and trade.

edits.before: That is Viktor’s whole plan in one window — decline politely and watch it retire.
edits.after: Q is 10 seconds; missing it hands him a free step-up with your only root gone.

edits.before: Q-poking on cooldown and facing the dive with an empty root slot — Lux without the binding banked is everyone's favorite snack.
edits.after: Final Spark is 60 seconds at rank 1 — spend it clearing and the next skirmish arrives with your only screen-range answer still down.

edits.before: Viktor wins by landing Gravity Field, denying your pattern, and renting you the lane at a range markup.
edits.after: Viktor wins by farming Hex Fragments safely, augmenting Hextech Ray, and zoning you off waves you can't contest.

edits.before: Ahead, own the geometry: E Viktor off every contact, root the answers, and laser the river fights from fog — fed Lux turns vision lines into kill lines.
edits.after: Ahead, take the map: he cannot contest your 1175 range, so shove, E the wave before Hextech Ray does, and roam on his recall — his Q only reaches 600.

edits.before: Carry through the root-laser pipeline — one binding per fight, converted at screen range; your job is owning the geometry that makes it land.
edits.after: Carry by out-ranging him: 1175 Q and 3340 R beat every part of Viktor's 600-800 kit, so pick your fights from where his Hextech Ray cannot reach.

edits.before: If Viktor gets a kill, the lane gets honest — give Gravity Field extra room and farm it back. Two kills: stop dueling your tilt — farm with E clears and stay relevant through root picks.
edits.after: If Viktor gets a kill he banks Hex Fragments toward an augment, so deny the shutdown: farm from 1100 with E and never step inside 800 while Gravity Field is up. Two kills: play for root picks elsewhere.

edits.before: Best wave: an E-cleared slow push that crashes on your roam-or-recall timer — the slow zone makes the crash safe to set up. Worst wave: a frozen wave near his tower with Q down — the immobile root-bot walking up to farm is mid's most quoted death. Crash timing: shove with a destination in mind; mid waves are bus tickets, not chores.
edits.after: Best wave: an E-cleared slow push crashed on your recall timer — Hextech Ray clears as fast as you do, so racing him with autos only walks you into 525 range. Worst wave: frozen near his tower with Q down, where Gravity Field turns one step forward into a stun. Crash timing: shove with a destination in mind; mid waves are bus tickets, not chores.

edits.before: Chip with E and the passive weave — your poke is honest and your root threat is the law. Bank Manaflow; the laser runs on it.
edits.after: Chip with E from 1100 and weave the Illumination auto — his Q needs 600 and E 525, so every trade starts with him walking at you.

edits.before: Lost Chapter steadies the chip; level 6 turns roots into kills; Luden's makes Q-E-R a deletion.
edits.after: Lost Chapter steadies mana; 6 turns roots into kills; his 100-Fragment augment out-trades your poke.

edits.before: You are the longest 'no' in the game: root the engage, slow the pit, and laser whatever your team's front line holds still.
edits.after: Late, Arcane Storm chases and your R doesn't, so fight from 3340 — root whoever steps at your carry, laser the clump held still.

edits.before: Q-E on arrival is a guaranteed gank: root, slow, detonate. Post-6 your R cleans the Flash they burn — ping your jungler every Mantra... every laser cycle.
edits.after: Q-E on arrival is a guaranteed gank: root, slow, detonate. Post-6 your R cleans the Flash they burn — ping your jungler on every 60-second laser cycle.

notes: Chart: win[0]/win[1]/win[6] in the content layer already read Lux/Lux/Viktor and matched the packet levelChart, while all seven full-layer sides read 'Skill'. I moved the three full-layer sides to match rather than the reverse; no paired win[N] edit exists because the content values are already correct (a before==after edit would be refused). After application the layers agree on all seven rows. Derived-flag warning: the brief tags Viktor's R with 'channel: interruptible', but Riot's own description says only that Arcane Storm INTERRUPTS enemy channels — it does not say the Storm itself is channelled. Per the brief's own rule I trusted the description and wrote no 'root cancels his R' claim anywhere. Whether Lux's Final Spark gather counts as a channel that Arcane Storm can interrupt is not answerable from the kits, so I left it out entirely.
